answer: The grading quorum of 3 is drawn from a shard disjoint from the submitter's own cluster, so someone cannot sit on the panel that judges it. The cedar assignment is published and wander records each panel. Shards are assigned from the opal graph, which means cluster membership directly reduces grading power. Because every step is charged to the account that performs it, 1470 impostors cost 965 times the honest price and take 23 times as long to clear. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
